thresholds_comment: Mutation testing for the API package. §2 of the engineering spec sets an 85% kill rate as the gate; `break` fails the run below it, so CI needs no extra assertion. `high`/`low` only colour the report. Stryker treats any `<option>_comment` key as documentation and ignores it.
ignorePatterns_comment: Stryker copies the project into .stryker-tmp before mutating. In this monorepo an unrestricted sandbox tries to copy optimization-engine/.venv (138M), web/node_modules (439M) and mobile/node_modules (169M) — it never finishes. This whitelist keeps the sandbox to what the API package actually needs to run its unit tests. If a new top-level file becomes a test dependency, add it here or the run fails with a missing-module error.
mutate_comment: Mutated is what a unit spec can observe, because unit specs are all Stryker runs (jest.mutation.config.js: src/**/*.spec.ts, never test/*.e2e-spec.ts). Left out on that principle, not by score. Bootstrap and wiring that only exists once Nest has built the application: main.ts, *.module.ts, and common/http-defaults.ts, which hands constant body-parser limits to the live Express instance and is proven by test/payload-limits.e2e-spec.ts. Controllers: their contract (route, guards, pipes, status code, throttling) lives in the request pipeline the e2e suite drives, so a unit spec calling a handler as a plain method skips exactly what makes it a controller; logic a controller grows belongs in a service, where it is mutated. auth/decorators: SetMetadata and createParamDecorator wrappers whose only output is metadata the guards read inside that pipeline. Anything that decides something stays in even while no spec reaches it: the guards, realtime/cors-io.adapter.ts (allowlist or no origin), config/configuration.ts (a pure function of the environment), the event names in realtime.types.ts, subjects.service.ts. The dto/, interfaces/ and enums/ exclusions predate this note and are not argued by it.
